highlights.title: Mercedes-AMG’s first ground-up SUV is a 1,150hp electric beast
highlights.summary: Earlier this year, Mercedes' AMG performance brand grabbed our attention with the GT four-door coupe, a souped-up sports sedan with three axial flux motors delivering over 1,150 horsepower.
body: It may even out-muscle the Porsche Cayenne Turbo Electric and Lucid Gravity.

The AMG GT SUV (say that five times fast) marks the first time in the performance brand’s 59-year history that it has developed a full-size SUV entirely in-house from the ground up. Scheduled to hit the US next summer, the new EV is built on Merc’s high-performance AMG.EA architecture to combine sports-car handling with full-size SUV suburban practicality.

It will be available in three trims — GT 53, GT 55, and the flagship GT 63 — with the top model delivering 1,153hp via the same three axial flux motors powering the four-door coupe. That beats the Porsche Cayenne Turbo Electric with Launch Control, which is sure to make for some awkward run-ins around Stuttgart.

Thanks to an 800-volt architecture, the SUV supports blistering-fast charging speeds up to 710kW on the 128kWh battery (GT 63 / GT 55) and 600kW on the 106kWh battery (GT 53). Drivers can charge 10–80 percent in 12 minutes or gain up to 450km (around 280 miles) of WLTP range in just 10 minutes. The 128kWh battery trims will have an estimated max range of 435 miles.

highlights.title: Kartal hails mentality after 'dream come true' run to Wuhan Open final
highlights.summary: Britain's Sonay Kartal says making her maiden WTA 1000 final at the Wuhan Open is a "dream come true," adding that the mental side of sport is "one of my strongest assets."
body: Kartal became only the second British woman, after Johanna Konta (Beijing 2016, Miami 2017, Rome 2019), to reach a WTA 1000 final with a stunning 7-6 (11-9) 7-6 (7-5) victory over Jelena Ostapenko.

The 24-year-old, playing in only her third tournament since returning from a back injury, saved multiple set points to punish Ostapenko, despite the Latvian hitting an astonishing 50 winners in the match.
Kartal will take on Maja Chwalinska in Sunday's final, live on Sky Sports Tennis from 11.30am, after the French Open finalist upset fellow Pole and former world No 1 Iga Swiatek 7-5 6-1.
"I've been shooting to get this far in one of these events for a very long time and to be able to do it this fast after so long out, is special.

highlights.title: Meta removes language that may have allowed it to scrape news sites
highlights.summary: After backlash, Meta is updating its terms again to remove language that suggested it could scrape content from sites, including news sites, to train its AI. Specifically, the following language no longer appears on the commercial terms page: … Meta may use any content from such domains, web pages…
body: Language that experts say allowed the scraping of news sites to train its AI has been removed from Meta’s terms.

Many, including Neiman Lab and James Grimmelmann, a professor of digital and information law at Cornell, interpreted it as an attempt to give Meta the right to use content scraped from sites to train its AI products for free and supersede blocking instructions in a site’s robots.txt file.

“We’ve heard you and want to clarify: the crawling terms we consolidated only applied to our ads and business products, and we’ve clarified that in the terms themselves. It does not change how Meta uses web crawlers. As always, content owners can use robots.txt to signal their preferences. This is not about scraping news sites, and these updates don’t give us new rights that supersede those preferences.”

highlights.title: Supercell brings Clash Royale to tabletop with new Kickstarter board game
highlights.summary: Supercell is bringing Clash Royale to the tabletop with Clash Royale: The Grand Arena, a board game developed with Maestro Media, set to launch on Kickstarter on October 20, 2026.
body: Designed by David Gordon, Ryan Rodriguez, and TAM, the game supports two to four players who can deploy cards, attack opponents and send their towers across two lanes.
Players will compete to destroy towers and collect crowns, the player holding the most crowns in the end wins.

The tabletop adaptation aims to retain several mechanics from the mobile game, including card-based strategy. Players build eight-card decks around a chosen champion, whose evolution card remains with them throughout the game. Players can upgrade or add characters to their decks between battles.

“Clash Royale has earned its place as a leading mobile strategy game by challenging players to think tactically, adapt, and outsmart their opponents,” said Andrea Fasulo, head of licensing at Supercell. “With The Grand Arena, our ambition is to honour that competitive spirit and strategic depth, giving fans a fresh challenge worthy of the game they love.”

highlights.title: ‘American Horror Story’ Actor Orlando Jones on Taking Over Lance Reddick’s Role and His Season 13 Prediction: “Somebody Gonna Die!”
highlights.summary: The veteran actor speaks with The Hollywood Reporter about his debut as Papa Legba in the Ryan Murphy universe, the witches' fight against Satan and the "magical" experience of sharing the screen with Jessica Lange and the returning Coven cast.
body: Among the many characters returning to American Horror Story: 13 is Papa Legba, with Orlando Jones taking over the role originally introduced in the horror anthology series’ third season, Coven, and season eight, Apocalypse, played by Lance Reddick, who died in 2023.

But this time, Papa is in an unusual position: he becomes the Coven’s ally and key source of information about Satan’s (aka Mr. Nas, played by Paul Anthony Kelly ) plan, a greater demonic threat, and how they can stop him to prevent the end of the world. The plan in question: Satan plans to leave Earth once his son, revealed to be Ben (Joey Pollari), claims his throne. So the witches must find the son to stop him from accepting the role. However, Ben finds them first, as episode 10 ends with Ben arriving at the Coven’s doorstep.

Below, Jones breaks down whether Papa can be trusted, the behind-the-scenes prosthetics, makeup and hair process behind his transformation, how “magical” it is to be set with the Coven women, especially with Jessica Lange ‘s return, his thoughts on the witches’ fate and more.

highlights.title: Elon Musk settles lawsuits over $1 million voter giveaway
highlights.summary: In 2024, Elon Musk promised to give away $1 million a day to a randomly selected registered voter in a swing state. That prompted legal challenges, raised questions about its legality, and drew lawsuits from two Arizona residents claiming the lottery was a fraud.
body: Plaintiffs claiming Musk’s $1 million voter lottery was a fraud are settling for an undisclosed sum.

The plaintiffs claim that when Musk announced the sweepstakes, he falsely claimed the prizes would be awarded randomly. Philadelphia’s District Attorney sued to stop the giveaway, claiming that Musk was running an illegal lottery. During a hearing, Chris Gober, a representative for Musk’s America PAC, told the judge that “The $1 million recipients are not chosen by chance … We know exactly who will be announced as the $1 million recipient today and tomorrow.”

That directly contradicted Musk’s claim that the drawings were random. The plaintiffs say they never would have signed the petition required to enter the giveaway if they had known it wasn’t random. They accused Musk and America PAC of using it as a ploy to obtain user data and said the petition “places no limitations on America PAC’s use of or sale of the personal data it collects, nor does it provide any additional information about the planned use of data.”

highlights.title: Websites are closing their doors to AI agents
highlights.summary: Autonomous agents are the hottest thing in AI. OpenAI, Meta, Google, Instinct, and others promise their agents can scour the internet on your behalf, doing anything from booking a dinner reservation and cleaning out your inbox to buying new shoes.
body: OpenAI, Meta, and Google want AI agents to do everything for you. But popular services on the web aren’t letting that happen.

In recent weeks, users of services like Meta’s Muse, xAI’s Grok, OpenAI’s Dots, and Instinct have reported blocks preventing their AI agents from performing tasks across top websites. Yelp told TechCrunch that it only allows AI agents that pay for its data licensing program, while Delta Air Lines is preventing them from booking tickets on behalf of users. JPMorgan Chase and Charles Schwab have also confirmed that they’re blocking AI agents from accessing accounts due to security concerns. Some users say sites that previously worked with their AI agent are no longer accessible, including Cars.com and Amtrak, suggesting other companies could be quietly blocking them.

highlights.title: My week wearing ankle weights: 'I was helping kickstart my muscles'
highlights.summary: When a knee injury forced me to change my fitness routine, I added Sportneer ankle weights – and got a decent workout. I’m a personal trainer. Here’s the equipment I use. Sign up for the Filter US newsletter, your weekly guide to buying fewer, better things.
body: M y exercise regimen has changed drastically over the last 15 years. A self-confessed cardio queen in my 20s and 30s, I alternated days at the gym with dance and Hiit classes and endured long bouts on the full complement of cardio equipment. And then my body caught up with me. First it was bursitis in my knee, which my doctor called “burpee-itis” from the ridiculous amount of the exercises I was performing. “You have to listen to your body,” he lightly chided as he poked at my swollen kneecap. Once my lower back started to complain, I had to start making serious concessions.

Thankfully, finding new ways to stay in shape was not as hard as I thought. A quick pivot led me to strength training, barre and pilates classes, and lots and lots of walking. My knee was still keeping me from doing a ton of basic leg work including squats and lunges, so ankle weights seemed like an easy solution. After doing some research on what would fit my specific needs, I decided on Sportneer ankle weights and used them daily for a week to see if they could enhance my lower body workouts.

highlights.title: Katie Zacharia Was Linked to an AI Rare-Earths Startup. It’s Even Weirder Than It Sounds
highlights.summary: The short-lived White House press secretary was listed as an adviser to a Kristi Noem–linked company that aims to use AI for mining. Both the company and she say she never worked there.
body: Before being fired five days into her stint as White House press secretary, Katie Zacharia spent much of the day attempting to explain her past.

Throughout her brief tenure, Zacharia’s résumé was the source of much intrigue. Foremost was the fact that despite claiming to be an attorney for much of her career, she never actually passed the California bar, as she was eventually forced to admit. Another element of her professional history, WIRED reported, was a role as an affiliate marketer for Beachbody, a fitness multilevel marketing company.

WIRED has now uncovered new details of her relationship to an AI-powered rare-earth mining operation called NRED Intelligent Mining, which counts former Department of Homeland Security secretary Kristi Noem as a strategic adviser.

On June 24, NRED—then known as NovaRed Mining, a small copper-and-gold exploration company in Vancouver, Canada—issued a press release to share that Zacharia, who had left a role as a DHS spokesperson two months before, was joining the advisory board alongside Noem.

highlights.title: Why Britain should reject the lure of cheap – and scary – Chinese AI
highlights.summary: In the west the technology comes with at least some effort to provide security and a benign intent – not so from China. There is much to fear from artificial intelligence developed in China and handed to businesses and governments in the west almost free of charge.
body: Every month Chinese AI developers such as DeepSeek and Xiaomi dispatch the latest versions of their “open-weight” models that allow users to take the core software and use it without paying an expensive ongoing licence.
In Britain, we love cheap Chinese kit, usually setting aside any concerns about how it was made and who by.

The row over whether to allow Chinese electric cars unfettered access to British retail forecourts is a case in point. They are cheaper than other EVs sold in the UK and, consumers ask: What is not to like? These same consumers might consider how Chinese EVs are subsidised by Beijing deliberately to boost exports and, in so doing, undermine foreign domestic car industries.
It’s scary because Beijing is entering a new phase in the long march of economic development, taking the world’s second largest economy closer to making China great again.

highlights.title: 7 Miles Out review – Carol Morley’s funny-poignant self-portrait of teenage kicks in Stockport
highlights.summary: A daring, rich and funny study of the ordeal of having to invent and reinvent your own teenage sense of self amid confounding changes. Carol Morley’s self-portrait of the artist as a young woman is rich, tender and terribly funny and sad: a study in the chaos of being young and a triptych of…
body: 7 Miles Out is based on Morley’s autobiographical novel of the same title, the once-upon-a-time-in-Stockport story of Ann, played with charm and zing by Lucy Halliday, and as a sweetly innocent young girl by Amelie Hughes. Young Ann pretends to be making a radio programme with her cassette recorder the way so many did in the 1970s, and hero-worships her would-be rock journalist elder brother Scott (Kasper Hilton-Hille) – based on Morley’s brother Paul – who is already plugged into the burgeoning post-punk and new wave scene.

Ann’s mum Bryn, wonderfully played by Gemma Whelan, is capable and good-humoured in a no-nonsense sort of way, but later to be beset with anger and mercurial depression. She has however found something to smile about now in the news that her husband and Ann’s dad Ronald, played by Aidan Gillen, has found a prestigious new job in Manchester – seven miles out. So to get to work, he has apparently been supplied with a handsome, though not brand-new car.

highlights.summary: With ia.i, a conversational interface, and the IARA governance platform, Itaú is applying its AI First strategy to customers and employees — in one of Brazil’s most regulated sectors.
body: Creating a close, personalized experience for millions of customers in a country like Brazil is, first and foremost, a question of simplicity rather than of models.
“Much of it is about making something simple, direct, and useful, delivering a direct benefit to the customer, and making the technology almost unnoticeable,” says Carlos Eduardo Mazzei, CTO of Itaú.

The standard he describes is demanding: the solution must solve a real everyday problem and be direct, simple, and memorable. Technology serves as the means, never as the centerpiece of the experience.

There is demand for this. A study by Itaú in partnership with Grupo Consumoteca shows that 80% of Brazilians want to better organize their financial lives and seek more effective support for decisions, and that 65% would like technologies that act as a financial copilot, providing ongoing guidance.

highlights.summary: True Detective fans just got some exciting news: two of the main cast members and the setting of the show's fifth season have been revealed. The casting announcements are especially exciting, as it has been confirmed that Nicolas Cage and Antonio Banderas will star as the headlining duo in Season 5.
body: True Detective has garnered a reputation as one of the best and most influential crime dramas on television, with its influence most recently being felt in DC Studios' Lanterns. Each season follows a different pair of detectives as they unravel high-stakes mysteries across the United States. The last season aired in 2024 and starred Jodie Foster and Kali Reis, but the first season, featuring Matthew McConaughey and Woody Harrelson, remains the most iconic.

If any pair of actors can challenge McConaughey and Harrelson for the True Detective crown, it'll be Nicolas Cage and Antonio Banderas. Variety reports that Cage's character is named Henry Logan, while Banderas will portray Rai García. We don't know much more about those characters, but it's safe to assume they'll be the detectives that the fifth season focuses on.

That report also confirms the season will be set in Jamaica Bay, which is part of Long Island in New York. We also know that production will begin in 2027 and that Season 4 showrunner Issa López will return to write, direct, and executive produce the fifth season.

body: Schwam co-founded Hanson & Schwam Public Relations with Adeline Hanson in 1955, establishing an independent publicity agency that would endure for decades.
Clients included Nancy Wilson and Lou Rawls, as well as the famous Coconut Grove nightclub, which helped the agency foster relationships with numerous entertainers.

His colorful representation (and intentional misreputation) of Presley in 1957 was covered in Variety at the time of the release of Baz Luhrmann’s “Elvis” in 2022. Schwam’s longtime relationship with Edwards extended beyond the professional. He was a friend as well as a publicist to the legendary director of such classics as “Breakfast at Tiffany’s,” “10,” and“Victor/Victoria.”

Edwards’ character of the neurotic publicist in his film “S.O.B.” was based on Schwam. That friendship reflected something fundamental about Schwam’s approach: he was known for his passionate engagement and resourceful guidance of his clients’ careers.

highlights.title: ‘It feels like the light is pushing the darkness apart’: Gellért Gombai’s best phone picture
highlights.summary: The photographer was holidaying with his family when two shadows became a plaything for his young son. Gellért Gombai, his wife and two children spend much of the year at their home in Budapest, Hungary, but most of their summers in Alsóörs.
body: On this particular day, the family had eaten hotdogs for lunch, before Gombai had taken the kids, Lóci and Janka, to the playground. “Lóci, who was five at the time, was jumping between two shadows – one from a changing room, and the other from a building’s roof,” he says. “I asked him to stay still for a few minutes while I got the shot, and he lay like this on the ground. He’s a big-hearted little clown; I’m so glad he’s my son.” When he showed the children, “Janka immediately asked me to take the same shot of her, which often happens. Lóci said it looked like he was among mountains, or as though a monster was about to eat him.”

Gombai applied his phone’s “dramatic cool” filter, and made some minor adjustments. “I really liked the slightly metaphysical spaces created by light and shadow,” he says. “If I forget for a moment it’s my son, I see a carefree form lying in the light while the darkness has bitten a large piece out of the space. Even still, it doesn’t feel sad to me. I have the feeling that the light is pushing the darkness apart.”

Combined with news that the FCC approved the deployment of 15,000 next-gen Starlink satellites and the company’s previous agreement to purchase close to $20 billion worth of EchoStar spectrum last year, it’s now clear SpaceX is serious about competing with AT&T, Verizon, and T-Mobile.

I’ve covered the telecom business for a long time, and I’ve always known that these companies can say they want to do something until they run into the harsh reality of how expensive it is to actually do it. The telecom graveyard of pivots, bad ideas, and failed acquisitions is vast.

highlights.title: US Representative Introduces Plan To Preserve Digital Game Ownership
highlights.summary: United States Representative Ritchie Torres will introduce the Power To The Players Act. This legislation is being made to support consumers' rights in a way that grants gamers ownership of their digital games.
body: Some companies are trying to preserve physical media and keep the disc format alive, but physical games are now endangered. With several publishers no longer selling physical versions, Sony ending disc production, and uncertainty around Project Helix's disc drive, the gaming world is headed towards an all-digital future, and gamers aren't happy.

Regardless of what the future holds for physical games, digital media currently dominates the gaming market. That is why Rep. Ritchie Torres wants to cement gamers' ownership rights over their digital libraries with the introduction of the Power To The Players bill.

At the moment, companies have full control of gamers' digital licenses. Digital storefronts can delist games, cutting off access to a wide audience within seconds. Developers can shut down servers if a game isn't as profitable as they had hoped, stripping gamers of online features promised on launch. As Torres puts it, families use their savings to purchase games, but with a digital license, the software that they paid for can be "pulled out from under them on a company's arbitrary timeline."

highlights.title: Île Seguin: This tiny island just outside Paris is about to become the city's newest cultural destination
highlights.summary: A sleek new contemporary art center is opening on Île Seguin this October, marking another milestone in the transformation of this former industrial site on the Seine.
body: Paris is hardly short of museums and is a real paradise for art lovers. Not only could you spend weeks hopping between its biggest hitters—namely the Louvre, Musée d'Orsay, and Musée de l'Orangerie —but the city also has an incredible collection of smaller museums and galleries that are less frequented by tourists, yet definitely deserve some love. If, like me, you have a particular soft spot for contemporary art, Gagosian and Perrotin are just two of the many galleries worth visiting in the city, and they're among my favorites to browse on a rainy Parisian day.

Although the city center has countless museums to visit, this autumn, one of the French capital's most exciting cultural openings is happening somewhere you might not immediately think to look: on a small island in the Seine just beyond the city limits.

Île Seguin sits at Boulogne-Billancourt, southwest of central Paris and around a 10-minute walk from the end of Métro line 9. Once synonymous with industry—Renault operated its enormous factory here for much of the 20th century—the island has been gradually reinventing itself as a cultural district. Now, the next major piece of the puzzle is about to be added.

highlights.title: Encryption Is Getting Squeezed From All Sides
highlights.summary: Canada’s planned surveillance law is the latest grim step in a series of threats to encryption that are spreading around the world.
body: Oh, Canada. The Great White North is the latest country to contemplate legislation that could essentially mandate backdoors and increase data retention in encrypted services. The proposed changes have prompted the Canadian anti-censorship company Psiphon VPN—which keeps millions of Iranians online during repressive internet shutdowns —to say it will leave the country if the bill passes. And Psiphon is not the only one.

Encrypted messaging app Signal has said it would exit the Canadian market because the legislation would require unacceptable changes to its open source projects. Apple and Meta have criticized the bill, and DuckDuckGo and NordVPN say they would consider pulling their services, too. But as countries around the world contemplate similar legislation, even larger questions begin to emerge about which states or regions could differentiate themselves as being safe havens for privacy services if global hostility to encryption continues to rise.

highlights.title: Fostering community amid Kendall Square’s innovation
highlights.summary: The 18th annual Kendall Square Association Annual Meeting explored how new technologies could be a force for shared prosperity in society.
body: Kendall Square in Cambridge, Massachusetts, is often cited as the most innovative square mile in the world. But when the Kendall Square Association gathered local stakeholders for its 18th Annual Meeting Thursday, the conversation focused on innovation primarily in the context of community.

The event, which took place at the nonprofit startup incubator The Engine, attracted people from across Cambridge, including business leaders, elected officials, local residents, and students, for a night of local food and conversation about the advance of technologies like artificial intelligence and what they mean for society.

“How can we make AI not an enemy of work, but a tool for workers to expand their capabilities and build new expertise or do new things?” asked MIT Institute Professor Daron Acemoglu in a keynote talk. “The world is at a point in time where we need new innovations and new adaptations to growing challenges.”

Acemoglu’s keynote was one of several presentations at the event, which also featured music from the Kendall Square Orchestra, a vote on new KSA board members, and awards for organizations making a positive impact through innovation.

highlights.title: 22 Years Ago, One Perfect Twist Changed TV's Greatest Sci-Fi Series Forever
highlights.summary: At the time, Lindelof was discussing his new series, Lost — which just four episodes in, had pulled off a mind-blowing twist arguably on the same level as The Sixth Sense. For its first few episodes, Lost seems like an ambitious survival drama with a dash of horror.
body: The best twists totally recontextualize everything that’s come before them. Mystery-box series master Damon Lindelof ( Lanterns, Watchmen ) once cited The Sixth Sense as the definitive example: The movie works if Bruce Willis is simply a psychiatrist helping a child who sees dead people — even if it’s a child hallucinating these haunting visions. The revelation that Dr. Malcolm Crowe was dead all along, however, changes not just the ending, but the entire movie. Lindelof told Vox in 2004 that the reaction is, “Oh, I didn’t even think I was sitting in that movie.” The twist makes The Sixth Sense “completely and totally transcendent.

This revelation doesn’t just help explain why Locke comes off as a bit strange. It suddenly forces viewers to reconsider every carefully framed flashback in every episode. It also establishes that the Island can literally perform miracles. The crash is an absolute tragedy that leaves everyone stranded and fighting for survival, but for Locke, it has given him a new life. When we learn the truth about his past, Lost transforms from a survival story into a spiritual mystery about destiny, magic, and faith.

highlights.title: How NBC Brought Live Musicals Back to Television
highlights.summary: In 2011, NBC was in a rough shape. The network had struggled in the waning years under General Electric’s ownership. In January 2011, Comcast became the majority shareholder, and with it came a new leadership regime for NBC Entertainment, led by industry veteran Bob Greenblatt.
body: Nobody — not even Greenblatt, Zadan or Meron — quite knew what NBC had until the opening moments of the production on Dec. 5, 2013. Within minutes, fans ranging from Tina Fey to Cameron Diaz to everyday people who love tuners were chiming in on Twitter with posts noting the joy of singing along with the beloved Rodgers and Hammerstein standard.
Greenblatt credits the late producer Zadan and his longtime partner Meron for picking “Sound of Music” as the one to roll the dice on.

“They thought it could bring in a huge audience since it’s beloved by adults and children and is constantly being produced all over the world,” Greenblatt says. “We had no idea how to even produce a live musical or how we could market it since it there hadn’t been anything like it in decades. But everyone at the network got excited about it and came together to turn it into a powerhouse.”
